We have mass spec: m/z 179.0946 (intensity 100). Likely molecular ion [M+H]+? Usually ESI positive gives M+H. So neutral mass ~178.0946. Formula? Let's compute possible formula. C? H? O? Let's see C11H14O2 has exact mass: C11=132.0000, H14=14.1096, O2=31.9898 total =178.0994. That's close to 178.0946 difference ~0.0048. Could be C10H14O3? C10=120, H14=14.1096, O3=47.9847 total=182.0943 not match. C9H10O4: 108+10.078+63.979=182.057. Not. C9H10O3:108+10.078+47.985=166.063. Not. So C11H14O2 seems plausible.

Carbon NMR peaks: 166.40 (likely carbonyl C=O of ester). 131.87, 129.70 (x2), 129.01 (x2), 129.00 (maybe aromatic). That's many aromatic carbons ~6-7 signals. Then 52.24 (likely O-CH3 or O-CH2). 43.47, 38.60 (alkyl). So structure maybe phenylpropyl ester? The carbonyl at 166 suggests ester. 52.24 could be OCH3 (methoxy). So methyl ester of phenylbutanoic acid? COC(=O)CCCc1ccccc1 matches formula C12? Let's compute: COC(=O)CCCc1ccccc1: that's methyl 4-phenylbutanoate? Count: phenyl C6H5, plus chain C4 (CCC plus carbonyl carbon) plus OCH3. Total C? phenyl 6, chain 4 =10, carbonyl carbon 1 =11, OCH3 carbon 1 =12. So C12H? Let's compute: phenyl C6H5, chain: CH2-CH2-CH2- (3 CH2) = C3H6, carbonyl carbon no H, OCH3 = CH3. So total C12, H5+6+3=14? Wait OCH3 adds 3 H, chain adds 6 H, phenyl 5 H =14 H. O2. So C12H14O2. Mass: C12=144, H14=14.1096, O2=31.9898 total=190.0994. Not match.

Our formula C11H14O2 mass 178.099. Could be phenylpropyl acetate? CH3COO-CH2-CH2-CH2-Ph? That's C11H12O2? Let's compute: phenyl C6H5, chain CH2-CH2-CH2 = C3H6, carbonyl carbon C1, methyl of acetate CH3 = C1H3, O2. Total C11? 6+3+1+1=11. H:5+6+3=14. O2. Yes C11H14O2 matches. So structure: phenylpropyl acetate (phenylpropyl acetate) i.e., phenylpropyl acetate: CH3COOCH2CH2CH2Ph. SMILES: CCOC(=O)CCCc1ccccc1? Wait acetate: CH3COO-CH2-CH2-CH2-Ph. SMILES: CCOC(=O)CCCc1ccccc1? Actually CH3COO is C(=O)OCH3? No acetate group: CH3COO- is C(=O)OCH3. But we have OCH2CH2CH2Ph, so O attached to propyl phenyl. So SMILES: CCOC(=O)CCCc1ccccc1? Let's parse: CCOC(=O) is ethyl acetate? Actually CCOC(=O) is ethyl acetate (CH3CH2O-C(=O)-). That's O-ethyl. We need O-CH2CH2CH2-Ph. So O attached to CH2 (propyl). So SMILES: CCOC(=O)CCCc1ccccc1 is ethyl acetate attached to propyl phenyl? Wait CCOC(=O) is ethoxy carbonyl, not correct. Should be OCH2CH2CH2Ph attached to carbonyl carbon: C(=O)OCH2CH2CH2c1ccccc1. So SMILES: C(=O)OCCCc1ccccc1 with a methyl on carbonyl: CH3COO... Actually acetate: CH3COO-... So carbonyl carbon attached to CH3 and O-alkyl. So SMILES: CC(=O)OCCCc1ccccc1. That is methyl? Wait CC(=O) is acetyl (CH3-CO-). Then OCCCc1ccccc1 is O-CH2CH2CH2-Ph. So full: CC(=O)OCCCc1ccccc1. Count: C: CH3 (1), carbonyl C (1), OCH2CH2CH2 (3), phenyl (6) =11. H: CH3 3, OCH2CH2CH2 2+2+2=6, phenyl 5 =14. O2. Good. So SMILES: CC(=O)OCCCc1ccccc1.

Check carbonyl carbon shift ~166, aromatic ~129, aliphatic ~43,38,52? OCH2 attached to carbonyl O maybe ~52? Actually O-CH2 attached to carbonyl O is O-CH2 (alkoxy) ~ 60 ppm maybe. Our 52.24 fits. 43.47 maybe CH2 next to phenyl, 38.60 CH2 next to carbonyl? Reasonable.

Thus propose SMILES CC(=O)OCCCc1ccccc1.

Validate.
